title: Deterministic Verification and a Single-Repair Guardrail for LLM-Generated Network Configurations: A Paired, Shared-Candidate Study
abstract: We report a sealed, preregistered paired experiment that measured the marginal verifier-detected effect of interposing a deterministic validator plus at most one automated repair on the same LLM-generated configuration candidate. Under preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics (one initial generation per intent reused for both conditions) we generated N_pairs = 250 constrained intent tasks with declared model gpt-5-mini and evaluated baseline (accept candidate) versus guarded (deterministic validation; if failing, permit one automated repair). Execution completed 500 episodes with model_calls_used = 251 (250 shared initial generations + 1 repair). Outcomes: baseline verifier-pass 249/250 (99.6%), guarded verifier-pass 250/250 (100.0%); contingency n11 = 249, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0; paired difference (guarded − baseline) = +0.4 percentage points (estimate = 0.004), paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI [0.0, 0.012] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729), exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. The single discordant pair was converted to pass by the single permitted repair. All execution and analysis artifacts are archived in the registered evidence bundle referenced in the Disclosure Statement.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are being explored as intent-to-configuration translators in network operations (NetOps), offering rapid draft generation of device CLI sequences. Stochastic generation, however, creates operational risk: syntax errors, incorrect command ordering, and policy violations can produce unsafe or non-functional device changes. Prior empirical and survey work shows LLM feasibility for drafting configurations while emphasizing the need for deterministic verification or human oversight [1], [2].

A common architectural response is a generate–verify–repair (GVR) pipeline that interposes a deterministic validator between generation and acceptance, and—optionally—bounded automated repair. Such guardrails reduce mechanically verifiable error classes (syntax, ordering, local-policy violations) but raise the empirical question addressed here: what is the marginal verifier-detected benefit of adding a deterministic validator plus a single automated repair when the same initial LLM candidate is evaluated both with and without guardrail (shared_initial_candidate semantics)?

This paper reports a preregistered confirmatory paired experiment that isolates exactly that marginal effect. By reusing the identical initial candidate across baseline and guarded conditions, the estimand is the paired success-rate difference (guarded minus baseline) attributable solely to deterministic validation and the single permitted repair. We executed N_pairs = 250 constrained synthetic/emulation intents, reconciled provider-call accounting, and present artifact-grounded inference and diagnostics.
sections.related_work:
Prior NetOps and LLM-evaluation literature motivates GVR architectures and documents limits of LLM-only correction. Empirical NetOps studies show modern LLMs can produce usable draft configurations in controlled settings but typically require deterministic checks or operator review to address syntax and local-policy failures [1], [3], [4]. Work on generate-and-verify and automated repair in programming and configuration domains reports that verifier-guided repair can increase detection and correction of mechanically checkable defects while remaining limited for deeper semantic correctness requiring richer external tests [5], [6].

Deterministic network verification and formal-analysis tools (e.g., Batfish-like approaches, header-space methods, topology modelling) are mature techniques for checking forwarding, reachability, and many local-policy invariants and are natural validators in GVR pipelines [4], [7]. Surveys and threat analyses emphasize that LLM-only self-correction is often unreliable absent dependable external feedback and that prompt-injection and retrieval-based adversaries are practical threats to LLM-integrated workflows [2], [8].

Our study differs by executing a preregistered paired design under shared_initial_candidate semantics, reconciling provider-call accounting (showing 250 initial-generation calls plus exactly 1 repair call), and archiving complete validator and repair traces to permit deterministic audit of the reported contingency counts and per-stage call accounting.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The experiment was preregistered (study_id study-cand-2026-LLM-verifier-sim2real-v1) and specified a confirmatory paired design with N_pairs = 250, generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate, and primary estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. The preregistration froze the single-repair policy, exclusion and contamination rules, and analysis tests (exact McNemar two-sided; paired-bootstrap percentile CI with 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). The preregistration artifact is archived in the evidence bundle.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics and reconciliation. For each intent exactly one initial LLM generation was executed and that identical candidate was evaluated in two episodes: baseline (accept candidate as-is) and guarded (run deterministic validator; if invalid, allow at most one automated repair and re-validate). This semantics isolates only the marginal effect of deterministic validation plus the permitted repair on identical generations. Provider-call reconciliation records hosted_model_call_event_count = 251 with stage_counts: shared_initial_generation = 250 and repair = 1; these reconciliations are archived and consistent with the reported model_calls_used = 251.

Task corpus, validator, and repair. A deterministic task generator produced 250 constrained intent tasks in a synthetic/emulation partition. Each task payload included initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and a difficulty label (medium/hard/very_hard). The guarded pipeline used a deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) that parses CLI sequences, computes parsed_command_count, enforces required_sequence ordering and workflow policies, compares a final_state snapshot to the expected_final_state, and emits normalized_configuration, violation codes, and a boolean valid flag. Repairs were deterministic template-driven transformations limited to syntactic and ordering fixes (reordering to match required_sequence, splitting combined commands, token-ordering corrections). By design no multi-iteration repair or human escalation was permitted; at most one repair call per episode.

Inclusion, contamination, and analysis. The preregistered exclusion rules removed items that deterministically prevented verification (vendor-parser failures) or contained credential-like tokens or denylist hits. In this confirmatory run no episodes were excluded or flagged: complete_pair_count = 250 and contamination_summary = 0 flagged episodes. The analysis used the preregistered paired_binary_analysis_v1 executor. Primary inference reported exact two-sided McNemar p-value and a paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI for guarded − baseline difference (10,000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729). All analysis inputs, code, and outputs are archived.
sections.results:
Execution and reconciliation. Execution completed the confirmatory partition with planned_episode_count = 500, completed_episode_count = 500, complete_pair_count = 250, and model_calls_used = 251 (250 shared initial-generation calls + 1 repair). The deterministic reconciliation artifact records hosted_model_call_event_count = 251 and stage_counts shared_initial_generation = 250, repair = 1.

Primary binary outcomes and contingency. Validator-scored successes: baseline_success_count = 249 (baseline_success_rate = 0.996) and guarded_success_count = 250 (guarded_success_rate = 1.0). Observed paired contingency: n11 = 249, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. The single discordant pair (baseline failed, guarded passed) corresponds to the sole exercised automated repair; observed repair-conversion rate = 1/250 = 0.004 (0.4%). Representative per-episode validator traces (archived) show parsed_command_count = required_command_count for passing episodes and include validation_before and validation_after snapshots.

Statistical inference. Exact McNemar two-sided test on discordant counts (n10 = 1, n01 = 0) returned p = 1.0. Paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI for guarded − baseline difference (10,000 resamples; seed = 1729) is [0.0, 0.012] (i.e., 0 – 1.2 percentage points). Estimate = 0.004 (0.4 percentage points). All numeric analysis outputs and bootstrap parameters are recorded in the analysis results artifact.

Diagnostics and repair exercise. Validator traces include validation_before/after, normalized configurations, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, and violation lists. Only one repair was generated and applied; its repair trace (archived) shows the repaired candidate satisfied the deterministic validation checks that the baseline candidate failed. No other repairs were needed. No episodes were excluded or flagged; missingness counts = 0.
sections.discussion:
Interpreting the near-null marginal verifier effect. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics and the constrained synthetic/emulation partition used here, the marginal verifier-detected benefit of inserting a deterministic validator plus a single automated repair was small: initial gpt-5-mini candidates satisfied the deterministic validator in 249/250 cases and the guarded pipeline converted the single failing candidate via the permitted repair. The paired-bootstrap CI upper bound (1.2 percentage points) provides an empirical bound on the maximum verifier-detected improvement for this pipeline and task scope.

Artifact-grounded reasons for a small observed gain. Three execution-grounded factors explain the small measured margin: (1) the deterministic task generator encoded constrained intents, allowed_touched_fields, and required_sequences that reduced ambiguity and favored well-formed CLI outputs; (2) the declared model (gpt-5-mini) produced syntactically well-formed, highly consistent sequences under these constrained prompts; and (3) the deterministic validator checks mechanically verifiable properties (syntax, ordering, final_state snapshot) and therefore cannot capture broader operational correctness (live protocol dynamics, cross-device emergent effects, vendor-implementation nuance) beyond the validator's model.

Power, baseline rates, and interpretation. The preregistration power calculation assumed a baseline pass rate ≈ 0.90 and targeted detection of a 15 percentage-point absolute effect with ≈80% power when selecting N_pairs = 250. The realized baseline pass rate (0.996) is substantially higher than assumed, reducing power to detect small absolute paired differences. Consequently, the confirmatory run's practical output is a tight CI-based bound on verifier-detected improvement for the studied pipeline and task scope rather than evidence against any large-effect hypothesis.

Operational implications and failure modes. These results do not imply validators are unnecessary. Instead they quantify marginal verifier-detected benefit in a specific constrained setting: (a) in tightly constrained emulation-style tasks and with a capable LLM, the incremental verifier-detected improvement from a single automated repair may be small; (b) validators remain essential to provide deterministic guarantees on mechanically checkable properties when task scope, vendor heterogeneity, or adversarial inputs broaden; (c) more expressive validators, multi-iteration repair policies, human escalation, or external dynamic tests (live reachability or forwarding-state checks) could materially change operational benefits; (d) the dominant failure mode observed here was ordering/token-sequence mismatches that a deterministic template-driven repair could fix in one pass; vendor-specific semantic mismatches and cross-device emergent errors were not observed in this controlled task bank.

Limitations and external validity. The confirmatory scope is limited to the synthetic/emulation partition and a single declared model and validator implementation; preregistered community and production-like partitions were not executed. The deterministic validator assessed mechanically verifiable properties but not live protocol-level correctness. Adversarial prompt-injection, retrieval-augmented generation attacks, and large-scale production heterogeneity were not evaluated. These limitations restrict generalization and motivate broader follow-up studies.
sections.conclusion: We executed a sealed, preregistered paired experiment under shared_initial_candidate semantics to measure the verifier-detected marginal benefit of deterministic validation plus one permitted automated repair on identical LLM-generated configuration candidates. In N = 250 constrained synthetic intent tasks, initial gpt-5-mini candidates passed the deterministic validator in 249/250 cases; the guarded pipeline converted the single failing candidate via the single permitted repair. Observed paired improvement = 0.4 percentage points (estimate = 0.004), 95% CI [0.0, 0.012], exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. These results bound the verifier-detected marginal improvement for the studied pipeline and task scope. All execution and analysis manifests, raw responses, validator traces, repair traces, and analysis artifacts are archived in the evidence bundle described in the Disclosure Statement.

disclosure_statement:
Human role and autonomy boundary: After an autonomy lock required by the CNSM Agentic AI Researcher track, the autonomous system performed literature search, study selection, preregistration freeze, prompt preservation, model calls, deterministic validation, permitted repair execution, analysis, drafting, peer-review, revision, and finalization without manual human editing of technical content. A human Research Director selected the broad topic family and performed pre-lock infrastructure development only; no human manually edited manuscript technical content after the autonomy lock.

Models, tools, and framework: declared model = gpt-5-mini; deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5; deterministic task generator = deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5; adapter family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Execution used a guarded generate–verify–repair flow permitting at most one automated repair per episode. Provider-call reconciliation records model_calls_used = 251 (250 shared initial_generation + 1 repair) with per-stage counts archived in the deterministic reconciliation artifact.

Preregistration and immutable prompt reference: the study was preregistered under study_id study-cand-2026-LLM-verifier-sim2real-v1 and the immutable master prompt used to initiate the autonomous run is archived as provenance/master_prompt.txt with SHA-256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba. The evidence bundle contains the archived preregistration, execution manifests, raw responses, validator traces, repair traces, and analysis artifacts referenced in this manuscript.
limitations: Confirmatory scope limited to the synthetic/emulation partition; preregistered community and production-like partitions were not executed and remain exploratory.

Deterministic validator assessed mechanically verifiable properties (syntax and prescribed workflow sequences) but did not measure broader semantic or behavioral correctness (protocol dynamics, emergent interactions).
Single declared model (gpt-5-mini) and one validator implementation were used; results do not establish multi-model or alternate-validator generality.
Only one automated repair attempt was permitted by design; multi-iteration repairs or human-in-the-loop escalation were not evaluated.
Adversarial and retrieval-based attacks (adaptive prompt-injection, vendor-targeted exploit vectors) and large-scale production heterogeneity were not exercised and remain open threats.
